topics.topic: How resend/recovery may use non-approval authority (grant or flow activation) when approval is missing or stale
questions: When a previously approved request no longer matches, and a standing grant is active, must the kernel always ask again, or may it send under the grant?

When resuming a `draft-write` element that is waiting on `service_unreachable` and has neither approval nor grant, should resend proceed under flow-activation authority or be forced into owner approval wait?
During restart recovery of an `in_flight` attempt whose authority is grant or flow activation, what record transition is required for authority usage?

quotes:
Any difference at send, whatever caused it (the inputs, or an
    instance's address or headers changed by a restart), asks again.

any difference, in an input, the instance's `api_base_url`, a required
   header's name or value or the credential header's name, means the approval
   is no authority for this send: it stays `approved` and unused, void when the
   run ends, and the kernel proceeds as if it did not exist — under a grant
   when one applies, otherwise by asking anew as rule 2 says;

`draft-write` nodes ask nothing at run time: K-08 lists the classes that stop
   for approval, and `draft-write` is not one; its authority is the owner's
   activation of the flow version (A06).

its authority is checked as it stands at the resume: its unused approval
   (M24), which is used first when both exist, or a grant still active; an element whose grant was revoked meanwhile
   waits for approval instead.

- `authority`: the approval or the grant it used, or for a `draft-write` send
  the flow activation under which the run started (State 2, A10 rule 6; State
  5) — except a resend after `not_applied`, which, whatever its class, records
  the fresh approval it needed;

and marks the approval the attempt names as its
   authority `used`, in the same store call, one call per attempt.
judgement.why: These passages prescribe incompatible authority handling for changed-request resend and restart recovery, so implementers cannot satisfy all of them at once.

topics.topic: What Content-Type multipart value parts use and whether it affects approval digest matching
questions: What `Content-Type` is sent for multipart value parts, and is it part of approval digest matching?

topics.topic: What URL components api_base_url may include and how they are combined into the final request URL
questions: Which additional URL components are allowed in `api_base_url` (path prefix, query, fragment, userinfo), and how must they be handled when building the final request URL?

topics.topic: What exact bytes are counted for MCP request-size enforcement
questions: What exact byte sequence is measured for MCP requests: transport/frame bytes, decoded JSON request bytes, or only the operation payload fields?

topics.topic: When to create a replacement approval request after approving a stale requested item
questions: After owner approves a stale request (digest changed), must the replacement approval request be created in that same owner action, or only when the run is advanced by a later request?

topics.topic: Whether compose_and_prove with unknown referenced IDs must fail as unknown-reference or proceed to proof failure while keeping flow version
questions: If composition payload names an unknown contract_version_id or binding_id, does composition refuse as unknown reference (keeping no flow version), or keep the flow version and return an unproven proof failure at phase 1?

topics.topic: Whether kernel-sent headers include runtime/library-added transport headers for request_digest handling
questions: Does "every header the kernel sends" include library/runtime-added transport headers (e.g., `Host`, `Content-Length`, `User-Agent`) or only headers explicitly set by kernel rules?

topics.topic: Which missing reference to report when multiple referenced records are unknown
questions: If one request names multiple records and more than one is unknown, which unknown reference must be reported?

topics.topic: Which rule-5 checks are re-run at send time and trigger binding_stale
questions: Exactly which rule-5 checks count as "of the record itself" at send time (and therefore cause `binding_stale`) versus checks that are not re-run there?
